title: Where ad frequency statistics are heading in 2026

facts.fact: Meta for Business's effective-frequency research found that a cap of roughly 1 exposure per week captures about 80% of total available ad-recall lift.
facts.quote: a cap of roughly 1 exposure per week captures about 80% of total available ad-recall lift

facts.fact: Meta for Business's effective-frequency research found that purchase-intent lift kept climbing until close to 1.5 exposures per week before slowing meaningfully.
facts.quote: lift in purchase intent kept climbing until close to 1.5 exposures per week before slowing meaningfully

facts.fact: Meta's brand-building guidance recommends aiming for a frequency of two or more exposures per week for campaigns built around brand-building rather than short-term recall.
facts.quote: recommends aiming for a frequency of two or more exposures per week for campaigns built around brand-building

facts.fact: Practitioner analyses of Meta data commonly report CTR decline above roughly 3.5 frequency in a 7-day window (this is a third-party claim, not a Meta figure).
facts.quote: CTR decline is commonly reported above roughly 3.5 frequency in a 7-day window

facts.fact: Conversion-rate and cost damage is described as clearer above frequency 5 in practitioner analyses of Meta data.
facts.quote: Conversion-rate and cost damage is clearer above frequency 5

facts.fact: Per the IPA's 2026 'Go Big or Go Home' report, fewer than half of surveyed CMOs maximize reach before layering on frequency.
facts.quote: fewer than half of surveyed CMOs actually maximize reach before layering on frequency

facts.fact: Per the IPA's 2026 'Go Big or Go Home' report, roughly nine in ten surveyed CMOs do not cap frequency at all.
facts.quote: roughly nine in ten do not cap frequency at all

facts.fact: Ampere Analysis data reported via Android Authority found average ad loads across major US streaming services rose 18% between January and August 2026.
facts.quote: average ad loads across major US streaming services rose 18% between January and August 2026

facts.fact: Ampere Analysis data reported via Android Authority found Netflix's measured ad minutes per hour rose 74% over the same January to August 2026 window.
facts.quote: Netflix's measured ad minutes per hour up 74% over the same window

facts.fact: Paramount+ runs roughly nine ad minutes per hour, per the page's citation of Ampere Analysis data.
facts.quote: Paramount+ now runs roughly nine ad minutes an hour

facts.fact: Disney+ and Hulu are in the 7.5-to-8.5 ad-minute-per-hour range, per the page's citation of Ampere Analysis data.
facts.quote: Disney+ and Hulu in the 7.5-to-8.5-minute range

facts.fact: A CTV benchmark referencing Innovid's 2025 measurement put average campaign frequency at 7.09 exposures across more than 95 million US households (a third-party benchmark).
facts.quote: put average campaign frequency at 7.09 exposures across a footprint of more than 95 million US households

facts.fact: Nielsen reach-efficiency research found average frequency climbs to six or more exposures once impression volume scales past 15 million, for campaigns without deliberate reach management.
facts.quote: climb from four or fewer exposures on smaller campaigns to six or more once impression volume scales past 15 million

facts.fact: The page cites an IPA/Gartner 2025 estimate that 30%-40% of marketing budget is misallocated to activation.
facts.quote: Share of marketing budget IPA/Medialab estimate misallocated to activation | 30%-40%

facts.fact: Google Ads does not publish one universal recommended frequency number; it documents frequency capping as an advertiser-configured setting at campaign, ad group or ad level.
facts.quote: it does not publish one universal recommended number

facts.fact: For Google Ads Display, only viewable impressions count toward the frequency cap.
facts.quote: only viewable impressions count toward the cap for Display

facts.fact: Practitioner guidance commonly anchors 2 to 3 exposures per week for Google Display and Demand Gen campaigns (not a platform-set number).
facts.quote: commonly anchors 2 to 3 exposures per week for Display and Demand Gen campaigns

facts.fact: Practitioner guidance commonly anchors 3 to 5 exposures per week for video campaigns built around recall.
facts.quote: 3 to 5 per week for video campaigns built around recall

facts.fact: Practitioner guidance suggests adjusting Google Ads frequency caps from account frequency-distribution reporting after roughly two weeks of delivery data.
facts.quote: adjusts from the account's own frequency-distribution reporting after roughly two weeks of delivery data

facts.fact: The page states that layering CTV on linear can lift unique reach by up to 32%, reducing repeat exposure (no source is given for this claim).
facts.quote: Layering CTV on linear can lift unique reach by up to 32%
